subject: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks
messages:
From: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, enterprise-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 08:12:00 -0700
Subject: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks

Team —

Attached is the consolidated March dashboard snapshot and a short bridge note highlighting anomalies that matter for next week’s QBR with Acme. High-level bullets:

- Latency: p95 increased from 310ms -> 420ms week-over-week on interactive routes; root cause looks like a bad kernel combo on a single host pool.
- Cost: token-unit cost rose ~9% month-over-month driven by increased burst traffic and a suboptimal batching profile for 2 large customers (Acme is one).
- Uptime: Service SLOs met overall (99.95%) but we saw a 12-minute degradation window during slot rebalancing on 2028-03-17 (post-release).
- Usage: Acme’s nightly batch jobs now dominate KV-cache usage between 02:00–04:00 PST, increasing tail-latency for interactive requests.

Action asks for leadership:
1) Markus: prioritize a quick kernel/quantization fallback for the affected model variant; ETA?
2) Laura: confirm whether we can offer Acme a short-term routing carve-out to limit their batch jobs to a separate pool during the QBR runway.
3) Jonas & Vivek: I want a 15-min ops runbook itemized for the 1-hour QBR slot to explain the mitigation plan and cost impact.

Attachments: dashboard-mar-2028-summary.pdf (2 pages), latency-cost-breakdown-202803.csv (table), qbr-prep-checklist.md

I’ll sync with Acme’s ops leads at 10:00 PT — adding enterprise-ops@acme-corp.com here so they see the note. Short replies OK — just want owners and ETAs.

Thanks,
Olga
Olga Petrov
Head of Observability & Ops
Redwood Inference

From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 09:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks

Thanks for the head's up, Olga.

Quick notes:
- Kernel combo: I can push a fallback to the previous kernel within 24 hours (safety window included). I want to run a 2-hour canary on low-traffic pools first.
- ETA for canary -> global fallback: ~36 hours if canary looks clean.
- I'll attach a short verification checklist and the canary rollout commands to the internal playbook.

One ask: if Acme needs the routing carve-out, we should pair with infra to ensure no collateral impact on other reserved pools. Laura, can you confirm whether a carve-out is acceptable contractually for a 2-week window?

-Markus
VP, Serving Reliability

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Cc: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, enterprise-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 10:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks

Olga / Markus —

From a commercial standpoint, we can propose a temporary routing carve-out to Acme as a complimentary mitigation for the QBR runway, but two conditions:
1) It must be time-boxed (max 14 days).
2) We need a short amendment (1 paragraph) accepted by Acme’s procurement acknowledging the carve-out and that it is a mitigation, not a long-term SLA change.

If Acme agrees, I’ll prepare an amendment and loop legal. Kelly (acme) — can you confirm whether procurement can sign a one-paragraph amendment within 48 hours?

Also tagging Jonas and Vivek to confirm operational feasibility.

Best,
Laura Bennett
Head of Customer Success, Enterprise
Redwood Inference

From: enterprise-ops@acme-corp.com
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks

Hi Olga / Laura / Markus —

Thanks for the heads up. Procurement (cc: kelly@acme-corp.com) can approve a 14-day carve-out amendment, yes — we just need the simple paragraph and an estimate of what the user impact will be. For the QBR, we’d like a short slide that: (a) shows the reduced p95 with the carve-out in place (expected), (b) the incremental cost delta, and (c) the rollback plan.

Kelly will coordinate on procurement sign-off. We appreciate the quick action.

—Acme Enterprise Ops

From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Olga Petrov <olga.petrov@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.ai>, enterprise-ops@acme-corp.com
Date: Thu, 29 Mar 2028 17:46:00 -0700
Subject: Re: March dashboard bridge note — latency/cost/uptime/usage & QBR asks

All —

Plan of record after internal huddle:
- Markus: begin canary rollout tonight to low-traffic pools (11pm PST). ETA for canary metrics: 2–3 hours. If stable, expand to full fallback by 12:00 PT tomorrow.
- Olga: I'll own the QBR slide pack items (p95 charts pre/post carve-out, cost delta calc). Will use the attached CSV for numbers.
- Vivek: please prepare the 15-min runbook script (who speaks when; 3 bullet mitigation notes).
- Laura: draft the 1-paragraph amendment and route to Kelly; we need sign-off within 48 hours to proceed with carve-out as a mitigation.

I’ll push a short Slack update to #ops-qbr and ping Acme’s Kelly after the slide draft is ready.

Jonas
Director, Inference Ops
Redwood Inference
